Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institu- 
1 11)11 on 25 September 1969^ after the draft finalized by the Fasteners for 
Consumer Goods Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consu- 
mei Prtjdut ts Divi&ion Council. 

0.2 In prepann^ this standard, considerable assistance has i been i derived 

from the fcjliownig 

53-GP-l7b Staplers and staples, paper fastening, office type. Canadian 
Government Specification Board, 

JIS-S 603 V 1965 Specification for staplers, Japanese Industrial Stan- 
dards. 

GG-S-74J3 Staplers and staples, paper fastening, office type, Federal 
Supply Service, USA. 

0.3 Clause 9.1 of this standard calls for agreement between the purchaser 
and the supplier and permits the purchaser to use his option for selection to 
suit lub requirements 

0,4 For the purpose of decidmg whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, express- 
ing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. 
'I'he number of significant places retained in the rounded oflT value should 
be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

3. TYPES 

3.1 The staplers shall be of the following types: 

a) Type I — Desk type: 

]) Light duty 
li) Heavy duty 
iiij Heavy duty, long reach 

b) Type II — Flier type 



IS: 5349-1969 

4. MATERIAL 

4.1 Vanous matf^riaJs empJoyed m the manufacture of staplers shall be of 
quality best suited for the purpose and these shall satisfy the requirements 
mentioned in the subsequent clauses. 

5. DESIGN, MANUFACTURE AND OPERATION 

5.1 Both types of staplers shall be designed for operation with the preformed 
Staples. The driving and clinching actions on ta a set of sheets shall be 
smooth and easy. After each stapling operation, the operating lever, 
staple driver and other connected components, shall spring back to the start- 
ing position and the base of vertical chute shall return to its norma] position. 
The feeding mechanism shall be spring loaded and it shall be capable of 
feeding subsequent staples under the staple driver after each stapling opera- 
tion Re/novable parts of all heavy duty stapJing machines of the same 
make and model shall be interchangeable, The^ shall be so constructed 
that the repair and interchange of parts may be possible. 

5.1.1 Springs — All springs used in stapler shall be made of spring steel 
Containing not less than 6 percent carbon conformmg to Section II of 

5.1.2 Staple DriveTs — Staple drivers shall be made of spring steel contain- 
ing not less than 6 percent carbon and hardened equally over the whole 
length to not less than 400 HV for light duty desk and plier type stapleis 
and not less than 490 HV for heavy duty staplers. 

5.1.3 Anvils — In case of Type I heavy duty staplers, anvils shall be a 
separate unit attached to the base. The anvil in heavy duty staplers shall 
be made of steel either hardened throughout or extra hard chromium plated. 
Hardness shall be not less than 700 HV, In case of T>pe I light duty or 
Type II staplers, the anvil ma\ be an mtegral part of the base. 

5.1.4 The desk type staplers and their anvils shall be designed in such a 
way that it shall be possible tu perfoi m the normal clinching, pmnmg and 
tackmg actions. 

5.2 Type I Desk Type Stapler — The stapler shall be constructed for use 
of preformed staples cemented m a scrip form. It shall consist of a base, a 
staple channel and a follower spring to hold the staples^ a staple driver 
attached to a plunger or striking arm, clinching anvil and other components 
fiiund necessarv for proper functioning and operation. Besides fulfilling 
the lequjrements m 5*1, it shall fulfil the lequiremenls mentioned m 5,2.1 
to 5.2.3. 



*SpecifiL-aiiun for steel wires for rokl forfued springs 

4 



15:5349-1969 

5.2.1 Range of Stapling — The range of stapling for the different desk type 
staplers shall be as given below: 

Range 



Light duty 50 

Heavy duty 100 

Heavy duty, long reach 200, 300, 400 

Heavy duty long reach staplers shall be provided with adjustable depth 
gauges, For hght duty, and heavy duty staplers a depth gauge shall be 
provided at the option of the purchaser. 

5.2-2 Vertical Chute — For desk type staplers, all parts of the chute with 
which the staples come into contact shall be hardened throughout or hard 
chrome plated to a hardness of 700 HV The surfaces of the vertical chute 
shall be sufhcjently smooth to provide easy passage of staples, 

5.2-3 Capacity — The light duty staplers shall accommodate a magazine 
of 50 staples minimum, Heavy duty, and heavy duty long reach staplers 
shall accommodate a magazine of 100 heavy duty staples. 

5.3 Type II Plier Type Stapler — The plier type stapler shall be designed 
and constructed for hand operation Besides, fulfilhng the requirements 
mentioned m 5-1, it shall fulfil the requirements given in 5.3.1 to 5-3-5. 

5.3-1 Jaw Opening — The jaw openmg of the plier type stapler m the 
normal position shall he^ 10 to 13 mm 

5.3.2 Stapling Range — The staplmg range or throat depth shall not be less 
than 30 mm 

5.3.3 Clinching Ann I — The clinching anvil may be an integral part of the 
base and shall produce a standard clinch 

5-3.4 Siaple Chute and Staple Driver — The staple chute of the pher t>pe 
stapler shall be formed by a separate piece of hardened steel fixed on the 
face of the chiite-end of the chdnneJ, ^fhe staple thute and staple driver 
mechanism shdll be so cnai,tructt*d as to t>perate without rloggm^ and 
jammmg, 

5.3,5 Capacity — The pher t\pe stapler shall hold a htjht dui\ staph' 
magazine contauiing a minimum of ^0 staples. 

6. WORKMANSHIP 

6.1 A]l staplers shall be free from burrs, sharp edges, imperfections and 
other defects which might affect its serviceability. 



15:3349-1969 

6.2 All metal surfaces shall be thoroughly clean and free from dirt, oil 
grease and moisture before applying the finish All metal surfaces shall be 
either painted or plated. The paint shall be stove enamel ( see IS . 150-1950* 
or IS 15Nj;55gtJ or air drymg enamel [see IS 2932-19b4:f or IS : 2933- 
1964§ ) of the specified shade. Prior to painting, all parts shall be degreased, 
rust-proofed and then protected by an anti-corrosive primer either by 
brushing or spraying and then finished. The finish shall be hard and shall 
not readiK chip or flake. The plating, if used, shall be cadmium znit or 
chronnum over mrkef. The cadmium piating shall be in accordance with 
IS: 1572-1960|| and the chromium and nickel plating shall be in accordance 
with Service Grade No 3 of IS ' 1068-1968*;, 

7. TESTS 

7.1 Performance Test 

7.1.1 Binding and Duzabihiy — A complete magazine of staples shall be 
mscriod in different types of stapler to produce the standard clinch. The 
number of sheets of 50 g/m^ white prmting paper conforming lo IS 1848- 
1961 ** for djflTerent types of staplers shall be cut and stapled for the number 
of times as mentioned below. After completion of the operation, the stapler 
shall not be jammed and the staples shall not show any malformation, that 
is, they are symmetrically towards left and right and the tips of staples are 
pressing firmly the paper surface tov^rards the ba^ side

7.2 Shock Test — All staplers shall he tested by dropping the machine 6n 
to a concrete floor or slab from a height of 90 to 100 cm. Machine shall be 
dropped so as to strike twice on top and twice on base, twice on 
opposite end of machjne and twice on both sides of machine. The machine 
shall not be damaged In any way bv this test 

8. MARKING 

8.1 Each stapler shall be marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or 
trade-mark, and with the leg size of staples to be used with the stapler. 

8.1.1 Each stapler may also be marked with the ISI Certification Mark. 

9. PACKING 

9.1 The staplers shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser 
and the supplier. 

NoTB — The uae of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Ruica and Regulations 
made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard 
convey! the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements 
of that standard under a well-defined system of mspcction, testing and quality control 
which if devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ZSI marked 
products art also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to (hat standard as a 
further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the ISI 
Gerti£cation Mark may be granted to manufacturcn or processors, may be obtamed 
from the Indian Standards UutiMition.
